record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.original_question: Describe the finite-dimensional real Banach spaces whose numerical index is 0.

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Describe the finite-dimensional real Banach spaces with numerical index 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space with dual $X^*$. The numerical radius of a bounded linear operator $T:X\to X$ is defined by
$$v(T)=\sup\{|x^*(Tx)|:\ x\in X,\ x^*\in X^*,\ \|x\|=\|x^*\|=x^*(x)=1\},$$
and the numerical index of $X$ is
$$n(X)=\inf\{v(T):\ T\in\mathcal{L}(X),\ \|T\|=1\}=\max\{k\ge 0:\ k\|T\|\le v(T)\ \text{for all}\ T\in\mathcal{L}(X)\}.$$
Give an intrinsic geometric characterization of those finite-dimensional real Banach spaces $X$ for which $n(X)=0$.
artifact.status_search_result: A partial result is known: a finite-dimensional real Banach space $X$ has $n(X)=0$ if and only if its group of isometries is infinite (equivalently, the Lie algebra of skew-Hermitian operators is nontrivial). However, an intrinsic geometric description of the finite-dimensional real spaces with numerical index zero appears to remain open, and the problem is listed as an open question in surveys on the numerical index of Banach spaces.

status_evidence.title: Finite-dimensional Banach spaces with numerical index zero (M. Martín, talk)
status_evidence.snippet: Talk devoted to finite-dimensional real Banach spaces with numerical index zero, discussing partial characterizations via the group of isometries.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of describing finite-dimensional real Banach spaces with n(X)=0 is studied and only partial characterizations (via isometry groups) are available.

status_evidence.title: The group of isometries of a Banach space and duality (Martín)
status_evidence.snippet: Relates the numerical index to the group of isometries; in finite dimensions, n(X)=0 corresponds to an infinite isometry group.
status_evidence.claim: Known link between vanishing numerical index in finite dimensions and an infinite isometry group, but no full intrinsic classification.
